# MusicTransform > Examples > Scope > Music Property Primitives > MusicInterval > 3

Invert an interval:

```wl
In[1]:=
m = MusicInterval["PerfectFifth"];
MusicTransform[m, "Inversion"]

Out[1]= MusicInterval[Association["Semitones" -> -5, "CentDeviation" -> 0, "Name" -> "PerfectFourth"]]
```

Note the interval direction is reversed:

```wl
In[2]:= %["Semitones"]

Out[2]= Quantity[-5, IndependentUnit["semitones"]]
```

Compound intervals (spanning more than one octave) return simple intervals (≤ one octave):

```wl
In[3]:=
m = MusicInterval[<|"Name" -> "PerfectFifth", "CompoundOctaves" -> 2|>];
MusicTransform[m, "Inversion"]

Out[3]= MusicInterval[Association["Semitones" -> -5, "CentDeviation" -> 0, "Name" -> "PerfectFourth"]]
```

</result>

<result url='https://reference.wolfram.com/language/ref/MusicTimeSignature#2033896159'>

# MusicTimeSignature > Examples > Scope > 5

Create a ``MusicMeasure`` object with a ``2 / 4`` time signature:

```wl
In[1]:= MusicMeasure[{"G", "A"}, <|"TimeSignature" -> MusicTimeSignature[2, 4]|>]

Out[1]=
MusicMeasure[Association["NoteList" -> 
   {MusicNote[Association["Pitch" -> MusicPitch[Association["Accidental" -> 0, "Key" -> "G"]], 
      "Duration" -> MusicDuration[Association["BeatDuration" -> Rational[1, 4], "Beats" -> 1]]]], 
    MusicNote ... cPitch[Association["Accidental" -> 0, "Key" -> "A"]], 
      "Duration" -> MusicDuration[Association["BeatDuration" -> Rational[1, 4], "Beats" -> 1]]]]}, 
  "TimeSignature" -> MusicTimeSignature[Association["Numerator" -> 2, "Denominator" -> 4]]]]
```

Measures in a ``MusicVoice`` can have different time signatures:

```wl
In[2]:= MusicVoice[{MusicMeasure[{"G", "A"}, <|"TimeSignature" -> MusicTimeSignature[2, 4]|>], MusicMeasure[{"G", "A", "B"}, <|"TimeSignature" -> MusicTimeSignature[3, 4]|>]}]

Out[2]=
MusicVoice[Association["MeasureList" -> 
   {MusicMeasure[Association["NoteList" -> 
       {MusicNote[Association["Pitch" -> MusicPitch[Association["Accidental" -> 0, "Key" -> "G"]], 
          "Duration" -> MusicDuration[Association["BeatDuration ... Rational[1, 4], 
             "Beats" -> 1]]]]}, "TimeSignature" -> MusicTimeSignature[Association["Numerator" -> 3, 
         "Denominator" -> 4]]]]}, "TimeSignature" -> MusicTimeSignature[
    Association["Numerator" -> 2, "Denominator" -> 4]]]]
```

</result>

<result url='https://reference.wolfram.com/language/ref/MusicTimeSignature#1496341221'>

# MusicTimeSignature > Examples > Scope > 4

Time signatures describing compound meter have a default ``"BeatLength"`` of 3 denominator units:

```wl
In[1]:= MusicTimeSignature[12, 8]["BeatLength"]

Out[1]= 3
```

Time signatures describing simple meter have a default beat length of 1 denominator unit:

```wl
In[2]:= MusicTimeSignature[4, 4]["BeatLength"]

Out[2]= 1
```

</result>

<result url='https://reference.wolfram.com/language/ref/MusicTimeSignature#1'>

# MusicTimeSignature

[EXPERIMENTAL]

MusicTimeSignature[n] returns a time signature with n quarter-note beats to a measure.

MusicTimeSignature[n, d] returns a time signature with specified numerator n and denominator d.

MusicTimeSignature[n, d, b] returns a time signature with specified numerator n, denominator d and beat length b.

MusicTimeSignature[…, properties] returns a time signature with the specified property association properties.

MusicTimeSignature[music, …] returns a time signature with properties inherited from another time signature music.

</result>

<result url='https://reference.wolfram.com/language/ref/MusicMeasurements#625098378'>

# MusicMeasurements > Examples > Scope > Music Property Primitives > MusicInterval > 3

Compute the distance in semitones of an interval:

```wl
In[1]:=
i = MusicInterval[5, <|"CentDeviation" -> 17|>];
MusicMeasurements[i, "SemitonesDistance"]

Out[1]= Quantity[5.17, IndependentUnit["semitones"]]
```

Compute the distance in cents (one semitone is 100 cents):

```wl
In[2]:= MusicMeasurements[i, "CentsDistance"]

Out[2]= 517
```

Compute the distance in hertz from a starting pitch:

```wl
In[3]:= MusicMeasurements[MusicInterval[5, <|"CentDeviation" -> 17|>], {"FrequencyDistance", MusicPitch["D5"]}]

Out[3]= Quantity[204.39772307087196, "Hertz"]
```

</result>

<result url='https://reference.wolfram.com/language/ref/MusicMeasurements#328999570'>

# MusicMeasurements > Examples > Scope > Music Container Primitives > MusicMeasure > 6

Compute the intervals between events:

```wl
In[1]:= MusicMeasurements[MusicMeasure[{"C", "E", "G", "A"}], "Intervals"]

Out[1]= {MusicInterval[Association["Semitones" -> 4]], MusicInterval[Association["Semitones" -> 3]], MusicInterval[Association["Semitones" -> 2]]}
```

Note that rest events are ignored:

```wl
In[2]:= MusicMeasurements[MusicMeasure[{"C", MusicRest[], "G", "A"}], "Intervals"]

Out[2]= {MusicInterval[Association["Semitones" -> 7]], MusicInterval[Association["Semitones" -> 2]]}
```

</result>

<result url='https://reference.wolfram.com/language/ref/MusicMeasurements#1417470103'>

# MusicMeasurements > Examples > Scope > Music Property Primitives > MusicInterval > 4

Compute the diatonic number of a simple interval:

```wl
In[1]:= MusicMeasurements[MusicInterval["MajorThird"], "DiatonicNumber"]

Out[1]= 3
```

Compute the diatonic number of a compound interval:

```wl
In[2]:= dn = MusicMeasurements[MusicInterval["MajorThird", <|"CompoundOctaves" -> 2|>], "DiatonicNumber"]

Out[2]= 17
```

Extract the diatonic number of the simple part of a compound interval:

```wl
In[3]:= 1 + Mod[dn - 1, 7]

Out[3]= 3
```

</result>

<result url='https://reference.wolfram.com/language/ref/MusicMeasure#98954582'>

# MusicMeasure > Examples > Scope > 4

Get and set the ``"TimeSignature"`` property:

```wl
In[1]:=
d = MusicMeasure[{MusicNote["C", 1]}]
d["TimeSignature"]

Out[1]=
MusicMeasure[Association["NoteList" -> 
   {MusicNote[Association["Pitch" -> MusicPitch[Association["Accidental" -> 0, "Key" -> "C"]], 
      "Duration" -> MusicDuration[Association["Duration" -> 1, "BeatDuration" -> Rational[1, 4], 
         "Beats" -> 4]]]]}, "TimeSignature" -> MusicTimeSignature[
    Association["Numerator" -> 4, "Denominator" -> 4, "BeatLength" -> 1]]]]

Out[2]= MusicTimeSignature[Association["Numerator" -> 4, "Denominator" -> 4, "BeatLength" -> 1]]

In[3]:= MusicMeasure[d, MusicTimeSignature[2, 2]]

Out[3]=
MusicMeasure[Association["NoteList" -> 
   {MusicNote[Association["Pitch" -> MusicPitch[Association["Accidental" -> 0, "Key" -> "C"]], 
      "Duration" -> MusicDuration[Association["Duration" -> 1, "BeatDuration" -> Rational[1, 2], 
         "Beats" -> 2]]]]}, "TimeSignature" -> MusicTimeSignature[
    Association["Numerator" -> 2, "Denominator" -> 2]]]]
```

If the total duration of events is shorter than the duration of the measure, a rest is appended:

```wl
In[4]:=
MusicMeasure[{MusicNote["C", 1 / 2]}]
%["NoteList"]

Out[4]=
MusicMeasure[Association["NoteList" -> 
   {MusicNote[Association["Pitch" -> MusicPitch[Association["Accidental" -> 0, "Key" -> "C"]], 
      "Duration" -> MusicDuration[Association["Duration" -> Rational[1, 2], 
         "BeatDuration" -> Rational ... ation" -> MusicDuration[Association["Duration" -> Rational[1, 2], 
         "BeatDuration" -> Rational[1, 4], "Beats" -> 2]]]]}, 
  "TimeSignature" -> MusicTimeSignature[Association["Numerator" -> 4, "Denominator" -> 4, 
     "BeatLength" -> 1]]]]

Out[5]=
{MusicNote[Association["Pitch" -> MusicPitch[Association["Accidental" -> 0, "Key" -> "C"]], 
  "Duration" -> MusicDuration[Association["Duration" -> Rational[1, 2], 
     "BeatDuration" -> Rational[1, 4], "Beats" -> 2]]]], MusicRest[Association["Duration" -> MusicDuration[Association["Duration" -> Rational[1, 2], 
     "BeatDuration" -> Rational[1, 4], "Beats" -> 2]]]]}
```

If the total duration of the events is longer than 1, and the time signature is not specified, the time signature is adjusted to accommodate all the events:

```wl
In[6]:=
MusicMeasure[{MusicNote["C", 7 / 4]}]
%["TimeSignature"]

Out[6]=
MusicMeasure[Association["NoteList" -> 
   {MusicNote[Association["Pitch" -> MusicPitch[Association["Accidental" -> 0, "Key" -> "C"]], 
      "Duration" -> MusicDuration[Association["Duration" -> Rational[7, 4], 
         "BeatDuration" -> Rational[1, 4], "Beats" -> 7]]]]}, 
  "TimeSignature" -> MusicTimeSignature[Association["Numerator" -> 7, "Denominator" -> 4, 
     "BeatLength" -> 1]]]]

Out[7]= MusicTimeSignature[Association["Numerator" -> 7, "Denominator" -> 4, "BeatLength" -> 1]]
```

If a time signature is specified, the total duration of the events needs to be shorter than or equal to the duration of the measure:

```wl
In[8]:= MusicMeasure[{MusicNote["C", 7 / 4]}, MusicTimeSignature[4, 4]];

MusicMeasure::measdur: The total duration of beats 7 exceeds the allowed number of beats per measure 4.
```

</result>

<result url='https://reference.wolfram.com/language/ref/MusicMeasure#366290585'>

# MusicMeasure > Examples > Basic Examples

Construct the music measure containing the specified notes and rests:

```wl
In[1]:= MusicMeasure[{MusicNote["G", 1 / 4], MusicRest[1 / 4], MusicChord["DMajor", 1 / 2]}]

Out[1]=
MusicMeasure[Association["NoteList" -> 
   {MusicNote[Association["Pitch" -> MusicPitch[Association["Accidental" -> 0, "Key" -> "G"]], 
      "Duration" -> MusicDuration[Association["Duration" -> Rational[1, 4], 
         "BeatDuration" -> Rational ... ation" -> MusicDuration[Association["Duration" -> Rational[1, 2], 
         "BeatDuration" -> Rational[1, 4], "Beats" -> 2]]]]}, 
  "TimeSignature" -> MusicTimeSignature[Association["Numerator" -> 4, "Denominator" -> 4, 
     "BeatLength" -> 1]]]]
```

</result>

<result url='https://reference.wolfram.com/language/ref/MusicMeasure#1302238491'>

# MusicMeasure > Examples > Basic Examples > 2

Construct the music measure with the specified time signature and key signature:

```wl
In[1]:= MusicMeasure[{MusicNote["G", 1 / 4], MusicRest[1 / 4], MusicChord["DMajor", 1 / 4]}, MusicTimeSignature[3, 4], MusicKeySignature[1]]

Out[1]=
MusicMeasure[Association["NoteList" -> 
   {MusicNote[Association["Pitch" -> MusicPitch[Association["Accidental" -> 0, "Key" -> "G"]], 
      "Duration" -> MusicDuration[Association["Duration" -> Rational[1, 4], 
         "BeatDuration" -> Rational ... on" -> Rational[1, 4], 
         "BeatDuration" -> Rational[1, 4], "Beats" -> 1]]]]}, 
  "KeySignature" -> MusicKeySignature[Association["Fifths" -> 1]], 
  "TimeSignature" -> MusicTimeSignature[Association["Numerator" -> 3, "Denominator" -> 4]]]]
```

</result>

<result url='https://reference.wolfram.com/language/ref/MusicMeasure#1'>

# MusicMeasure

[EXPERIMENTAL]

MusicMeasure[{event1, event2, …}] returns a musical measure that contains the musical events eventi.

MusicMeasure[events, ts, ks] returns a musical measure with time signature ts and key signature ks.

MusicMeasure[events, ts, ks, properties] returns a musical measure with the specified property association properties.

MusicMeasure[music, events, ts, ks, properties] returns a musical measure with properties inherited from another measure music.

</result>

<result url='https://reference.wolfram.com/language/ref/MusicInterval#295780291'>

# MusicInterval > Examples > Properties & Relations

Compute the frequency distance of an interval from a given starting pitch using ``MusicMeasurements`` :

```wl
In[1]:= i = MusicInterval["PerfectFourth"]

Out[1]= MusicInterval[Association["Name" -> "PerfectFourth"]]

In[2]:= MusicMeasurements[i, {"FrequencyDistance", MusicPitch["A5"]}]

Out[2]= Quantity[294.6590716696303, "Hertz"]
```

</result>

<result url='https://reference.wolfram.com/language/ref/MusicInterval#1314114019'>

# MusicInterval > Details

* ``MusicInterval`` represents the distance between two musical pitches, describing intervals by size and quality.

* ``MusicInterval`` represents the distance between two musical pitches.

* The interval distance ``d`` can be specified using:

|      |                                                     |
| ---- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| name | a named diatonic music interval (e.g. "MajorThird") |
| n    | the number of semitones spanned by the interval     |

* Use ``MusicInterval["Names"]`` to list supported interval names.

* The association ``properties`` can contain the following keys:

|                   |                                                   |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| "CentDeviation"   | cents difference from a whole number of semitones |
| "CompoundOctaves" | integer number of whole octaves in the interval   |
| "Name"            | common diatonic name of the interval              |
| "Semitones"       | number of chromatic steps in the interval         |

* For a music interval object ``obj``, any of the above properties can be obtained using ``obj["prop"]``. Use ``obj["PropertyAssociation"]`` to retrieve the values of all available properties.

</result>

<result url='https://reference.wolfram.com/language/ref/MusicInterval#1034599102'>

<result url='https://reference.wolfram.com/language/ref/MusicDuration#173838819'>

# MusicDuration > Examples > Scope > 5

Construct an eighth note duration with a multiplier of 2/3, or a eighth note triplet:

```wl
In[1]:= MusicDuration[1 / 8, 2 / 3]

Out[1]= MusicDuration[Association["Duration" -> Rational[1, 8], "Multiplier" -> Rational[2, 3]]]
```

Construct the same duration using its name:

```wl
In[2]:= MusicDuration["eighth triplet"]

Out[2]=
MusicDuration[Association["Duration" -> Rational[1, 8], "Multiplier" -> Rational[2, 3], 
  "Name" -> "Eighth-note triplet"]]
```

</result>

<result url='https://reference.wolfram.com/language/ref/MusicDuration#1314114019'>

# MusicDuration > Details

* ``MusicDuration`` is used to express the time occupied by musical events such as notes, chords and rests. It can be expressed as a note value or beats.

* ``MusicDuration`` is used to express the time occupied by musical events such as ``MusicNote``, ``MusicRest`` and ``MusicChord``.

* Possible values for the duration specification ``dur`` are:

|       |                                             |
| ----- | ------------------------------------------- |
| d     | note value as a real number                 |
| name  | named duration (e.g. "Quarter" or "Whole")  |
| beats | Quantity of type "Beats"                    |
| s     | Quantity of type "Seconds"                  |
| note  | a MusicNote, MusicRest or MusicChord object |

* A real-valued duration corresponds to a fraction of a ``"Whole"`` note value defined as ``1``. As an example, a duration of ``1 / 4`` corresponds to a ``"Quarter"`` note value.

* The association ``properties`` can contain the following keys:

|                |                                                   |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| "BeatDuration" | duration of a beat, related to MusicTimeSignature |
| "Beats"        | nominal duration in beats                         |
| "Duration"     | nominal duration as a fraction of a whole note    |
| "Multiplier"   | tuplet multiplier on the nominal duration         |
| "RealBeats"    | beats including tuplet multiplier                 |
| "RealDuration" | duration including tuplet multiplier              |

* For a music duration object ``obj``, any of the above properties can be obtained using ``obj["prop"]``. Use ``obj["PropertyAssociation"]`` to retrieve the values of all available properties as an ``Association``.

* A ``MusicDuration`` object can represent a duration in terms of note value or beats. The two representations are linked by the ``"BeatDuration"`` property, which indicates what note value a beat corresponds to. This can be useful in compound time signatures such as ``6 / 8``, where a beat typically corresponds to three eighth notes.

* ``MusicDuration[dur, mult]`` is typically used to express tuplet durations. For example, an eighth note triplet duration can be expressed as ``MusicDuration[1 / 8, 2 / 3]``.

* The ``"RealDuration"`` and ``"RealBeats"`` properties are computed as the ``"Duration"`` and ``"Beats"`` properties multiplied with the ``"Multiplier"`` property, respectively.

</result>
